title: IANA tz database: recovery map for hard-dead citations

method.dead_set: 349 URLs, from the 1,391 unique URLs cited in tzdb 2026c, that returned HTTP 404/410 or whose domain no longer resolves (surveyed 2026-09-06). 403/timeout/5xx were excluded as possibly bot-blocking rather than dead.
method.lookup: archive.org /wayback/available with timestamp = the citation date, taking the closest available snapshot.
method.fragment_handling: URLs carrying a '#' fragment were retried without it, since the fragment is not part of what the archive stores. This recovered 6 further citations, all Israeli official regulations.
method.citation_date: heuristic: the nearest preceding '# From X (YYYY-MM-DD)' attribution header in the same file. Confidence is 'high' when that header is within 40 lines, 'low' otherwise (61 of 349).
method.verification: 20 recovered snapshots were sampled and refetched in raw (id_) form, bypassing the archive's toolbar. All 20 returned the real captured document and their <title> matched the subject of the surrounding tzdb comment. No soft-404s in the sample. The remaining recoveries are unverified.

caveats: A snapshot far from the citation date may not be the revision that was cited. snapshot_gap_days is given so a reviewer can judge; the median is 149 days but the 90th percentile is about 6 years.
'recovered' means the Internet Archive returned a 2xx capture, not that the capture has been read and confirmed to support the tzdb row it is attached to.
Line numbers are for tzdb 2026c and will drift.
This is an outside survey. Nothing here has been proposed to tz upstream.

citations.cited_by: Peter Apps and Ranga Sirila of Reuters
